title: Homecoming and Recipe
premise: Oscar Vane, seventeen, has spent a decade keeping her three younger siblings fed, hidden, and safe while their mother works hospital night shifts — careful to the point of invisibility. When her college application demands one unguarded truth, the essay she writes in secret begins circulating, threatening the fragile story her family survives on. As she chases a culinary scholarship that could finally secure them all, Oscar must choose between protecting the lie that holds them together and telling the truth that might set them free — winning both championships before time runs out. In the end, she wins the competition but loses the scholarship on a technicality, and discovers the family she built by hand is worth more than any door it opens.
about_author: Xanthe Iversen grew up above a diner in a rust-belt town, where she learned that recipes are just stories you can eat. She writes young adult novels about kids who parent their parents and still find reasons to laugh.

chapters.title: The Careful Years
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A single day in the Vane household: breakfast made from nothing, homework supervised, lies told to a social worker at the door. We see Oscar's meticulous systems for survival and her siblings' quiet dependence on her. Emotional beat: love expressed as control, and the first hairline crack — youngest sibling Junie asks why they never talk about Dad.

chapters.title: One Honest Question
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The college essay prompt lands: 'Describe a truth that cost you something.' Late at night, unable to sleep, Oscar writes three pages she never intends to submit — about the night her father left, and what her mother really does with the missing hours. Emotional beat: terrifying relief; the secret has weight, and now it's on paper.

chapters.title: What Junie Saw
chapters.summary: Junie's POV (age nine). Junie finds the essay pages in Oscar's backpack and reads them aloud to middle sister Bea as a bedtime story, not understanding what she's holding. Beat: innocence as accidental detonator; the reader knows what the sisters don't.

chapters.title: The Scholarship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The regional young chefs' championship offers a full culinary scholarship — but its rules require family interviews and financial disclosure, which could expose everything. Oscar enters anyway, telling herself it's just practice. Beat: hope arriving dressed as risk.

chapters.title: Bea Keeps Score
chapters.summary: Bea's POV (fifteen). Bea, sharp and resentful, confronts Oscar: she read the essay, she knows Mom's night shifts don't add up, and she's furious at being managed instead of trusted. Beat: loyalty vs. truth turns inward — the family's real fracture isn't the secret, it's who gets to carry it.

chapters.title: Prelims
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The championship preliminary round: Oscar cooks a dish built from their family's poverty food and stuns the judges. But a classmate recognizes her essay's phrasing from a leaked draft online. Beat: triumph undercut by exposure closing in; the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Mom Comes Home Early
chapters.summary: Alternating Oscar and Mom POV. Their mother, Elena, discovers the leaked essay and the championship entry form. Instead of rage, she confesses the truth the essay only guessed at — the debts, the second job, the years she let Oscar be the parent. Beat: guilt met with grace; the lie dissolves from the top down.

chapters.title: The Championship That Does
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Finals day. Oscar cooks not to escape her family but to honor it, with Bea and Junie in the audience for the first time. She wins — then learns the scholarship board disqualified her over the disclosure irregularities. Beat: climax; victory and loss in the same breath.

chapters.title: What the Essay Was For
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Devastated, Oscar submits the honest essay — the real one — to the college, expecting rejection. A admissions reader calls instead: the essay is the reason she's admitted, with need-based aid no competition could have matched. Beat: the price of survival was never the truth; it was paying it alone.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Full-family POV rotation across one dinner. Elena takes a day shift; Bea takes over Tuesday dinners; Junie sets a fourth plate out of habit, then smiles because everyone's actually there. Oscar leaves for college knowing the home she built will hold without her hands on every seam. Beat: found family confirmed as chosen, daily work — bittersweet, warm, earned.
